title: Your First Week at GVC
short_answer: Who we are, who to call, what to open on your phone, and the non-negotiables that keep you — and the company — out of trouble.
summary: Day one through day five: learn how we decide, where the truth lives, and when to stop and ask. Speed without that is expensive.
plain_words: Green Valley Contractors builds walls and ceilings: metal framing, drywall, insulation, ACT, paint, demo, and patch. We work in Ohio, Indiana, and Kentucky. Your first week is not about being fast — it is about learning how we decide, where the truth lives (drawings + Job Start packet + Job Check), and when to stop and ask. Speed without that is expensive.

tools.name: Field Manual / Field Guide on phone
Job Check (observe a save before you tap yourself)

steps.title: Glossary
steps.body: Read the Glossary once in the Field Manual index — half the manual opens up after you know what "on center," "butt joint," and "raking light" mean.

steps.title: Reading Drawings
steps.body: Read Reading Drawings in Plain mode. Never scale with a ruler; find the sheet that owns the answer.

steps.title: Spotting a Change Order
steps.body: Read Spotting a Change Order. If it is not on our drawings, stop, photo, write it down, call.

steps.title: Safety Orientation
steps.body: Complete Safety Orientation before you climb, cut, sand, or demo anything unsupervised.

steps.title: Portal tools
steps.body: Open the portal on your phone: Field Manual, Job Check, Morning Brief, Time Off — start with Portal Tools for the Field.

steps.title: Shadow one stage
steps.body: Shadow one full stage with a lead — stocking, hang, scrape, or finish — and ask why each step exists.

steps.title: Job Check save
steps.body: Watch a Job Check save — pick the job, change only what you did, Save once. Monday is the office truth.

steps.title: QC walk
steps.body: Walk a QC pass with a lead under raking light. See what "done" actually looks like before you claim a stage.

warnings.title: The chain of call
warnings.body: Crew → your lead → superintendent / ops lead → office (scope and money) → owner only for owner-level exceptions. Skipping the chain wastes time and gets people conflicting answers.

warnings.title: Non-negotiables from day one
warnings.body: Never guess on a rated wall, shaftwall, or firestop. Never invent scope or promise the GC we will "just take care of it." Never skip the stop when work is not on our drawings. Asking is the job.

variations.title: Laborer / helper reading path
variations.when: First week on a helper lane
changes: Stocking Any Material → Stocking Drywall → Scraping → Clean-Out → QC Walk

variations.title: Hanger reading path
changes: Drawings → Pre-Board Walk → Hanging → Scraping → Insulation

variations.title: Lead (new to GVC) reading path
variations.when: First week as a lead carpenter new to GVC
changes: Change Order → Lead Day → Portal Tools → Rated Walls → Firestop → Framing → Hang → Finish

quality_checks.prompt: Reading Drawings completed in Plain mode
Safety Orientation read before unsupervised cut/sand/climb/demo
Portal tiles opened and Job Check save observed
QC walk under raking light with a lead

common_mistakes.title: Speed before judgment
common_mistakes.wrong: Start production before reading drawings and CO rules
common_mistakes.right: Complete the Day 1–5 checklist in order
common_mistakes.why: Rework and free work cost more than a slow first week

common_mistakes.title: Skipping the chain of call
common_mistakes.wrong: Call the office or owner for a field layout question
common_mistakes.right: Lead first, then ops, then office for scope/money

common_mistakes.title: Guessing on rated work
common_mistakes.wrong: Patch or frame a rated wall from habit
common_mistakes.right: Stop and read Fire Walls and Firestopping

provenance.note: GVC practice. This page is an orientation path, not an HR handbook and not a signed safety acknowledgment. Written programs (respiratory protection, silica exposure control, hazcom) live with the office; the field's job is to recognize stop conditions and escalate.
